summary: Anuj Misra studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker around 2012–2016.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a PhD from the University of Calcutta under Nalinaksha Dutt and Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya. He held faculty posts at Calcutta and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1981–1982).
Anuradha Seneviratna was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Peradeniya (c. 1964–1968) and later served there as a professor from around 1970 to 2004.

Archibald Edward Gough worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Monier Monier-Williams (c. 1864–1866). He held professorships at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (c. 1868–1878), Presidency University (c. 1878–1895), and Presidency College, Chennai, and served as Principal of Aliah University (c. 1881–1895).
Ariane Macdonald, a scholar of Tibetology and Sinology, studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. In 1972, she held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Arindam Chakrabarti specializes in philosophy and Indology and earned a DPhil from the University of Oxford. He served as a professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaiʻi (attested 2009–2014).

Arinde L. Jonker specializes in Indology and religious studies, completing a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and also studying under Daniele Cuneo and Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

Arjo Vanderjagt studied at the University of Groningen (1971–1981), where he later held a post in philosophy from 1994 to 2009. He also held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979) and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths studied at Harvard (1997–1998) and earned his PhD at Leiden University (c. 2001–2004) under Henk Bodewitz. Working in Indology, linguistics, and archaeology, he held posts at Groningen, Leiden, and the École Française d'Extrême-Orient (from 2008).

Historian Arnold J. Toynbee studied at Winchester College and Balliol College, Oxford. He held posts at King's College London (c. 1919–1924) and served as director at Chatham House while at the London School of Economics (c. 1925–1955).

Arthur Anthony Macdonell, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at Oxford, Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, and Leipzig. He was the Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1888 and a fellow of Balliol College from 1899.

Arthur Berriedale Keith, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford, under Julius Eggeling and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office before becoming a professor at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen, a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics, studied at the University of Copenhagen (c. 1893–1903) and under Friedrich Carl Andreas. He held the first chair of Orientalistics at Copenhagen from 1919 to 1945.

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at King's College London and under Theodor Goldstücker, Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and Heinrich August Jäschke. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1860 to 1880.
Arthur Evans was an archaeologist who was educated at Harrow School and Brasenose College, matriculating in 1870.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies, studying at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He taught at Stanford University (1947–1958) before serving as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale (1959, 1961).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian who earned his degrees at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He served as Professor at SOAS (1957–1965) and later headed the Asian Civilizations department at the Australian National University (c. 1965–1978).
Arthur McKeown is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Harvard University (attested 2005) under Parimal G. Patil, Palri Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer, a philosopher, studied at Göttingen, Berlin (under Fichte, Schleiermacher, Boeckh, and Wolf), and Jena, where he earned his doctorate in 1813. He also studied under Friedrich Majer and held a lectureship at the University of Berlin in 1820.
